tam.headline: The three Caribbean crossings are the floor — Mexico's water-crossing market runs far higher

rungs.label: What the three Caribbean crossings support today
rungs.note: Navier's annual revenue across the three sourced Quintana Roo crossings at full fleet (88 boats). This is the grounded floor, not the whole market.

rungs.label: Matured Mexico network Navier can serve
rungs.note: Navier's own transport revenue once the full addressable Mexican network runs at leading-operator capture, with faster, more comfortable boats growing the market. Mid case shown with a low-high range.

rungs.label: Mexico marine-mobility opportunity
rungs.note: Total annual water-transfer spend the induced Mexican crossing market can support at full network width.

rungs.label: Whole-journey value across those crossings
rungs.note: Door-to-door value of every journey that includes one of these crossings — the full trip DiDi's app coordinates end to end, not only the boat leg.

rungs.label: DiDi platform revenue on the Navier network
rungs.note: DiDi's platform take on the journey value routed through the Navier network, at DiDi's standard 18% commission.

rules.unit_economics_route: single representative exact-bound route; all values bound from the aggregate, never hand-typed
rules.tam_source: SOM floor from aggregate grounded_floor_by_market; SAM/marine-TAM/journey-GMV/platform rungs from finance/model/growth.py LB-254 ladder on the Mexico pool (see tam.source)
rules.fare_basis: premium-substitute (Uber Black $30 comparable), Jaideep-approved 2026-07-17; conservative for the longer Cozumel leg
